questions.question: Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts are found in different parts of India. Which of the following is NOT a find spot of Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts in Karnataka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rupnath.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rupnath inscription is near Kaimur hills, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• **Maski** inscription is in the **Raichur district, Karnataka.**
 
• **Gavimath** is in **Koppal district, Karnataka.**
 
• **Brahmagiri inscription** is in **Chitradurga district, Karnataka.**
 
• **Minor Rock Edicts of Ashoka:**
 
 
• These rock inscriptions are from the **earliest part of the Edicts of Ashoka.**
 
• **They predate Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts.**
 
• These are the **first edicts in the Indian language of Emperor Ashoka, written in the Brahmi script.**
 
• The **Kandahar Bilingual Rock Inscription,** in Greek and in Aramaic, is the** first known inscription of Ashoka.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• The Rock Edicts were the** first tangible evidence of, how Buddhism spread.** 
 
• These edicts were** deciphered by the British archaeologist and historian James Prinsep.**
 
• They were** kept in public places and along trade routes** so that the maximum number of people would read them.
 
• There are 33 inscriptions classified into the following categories:
 
 
• **Major rock edicts**
 
• **Minor rock edicts**
 
• **Separate rock edicts**
 
• **Major pillar edicts **
 
• **Minor pillar edicts**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka**

 
 
• Son of Bindusara and a Mauryan ruler.
 
• ​He was one of the **greatest rulers known in the history of India.**
 
• He has his inscriptions were **carved on pillars, as well as on rock surfaces** to connect with people.
 
• **The Kalinga War in 261 B.C** changed his heart and he started following Buddhism.
 
• Dhamma is a set of edicts that formed a policy of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka.

questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was repealed during the tenure of Viceroy _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Ripon.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Rippon repealed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878.**
 
• The viceroy feared that the** act may produce resentment among Indians.**
 
• **The act can become one of the catalysts giving rise to India's growing independence movement.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Vernacular Press Act: **

 
 
• Passed in 1878,** to restrict the freedom of the press of Indian languages.**
 
• Lord Lytton was highly criticized for the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878–80).
 
• **Aim to prevent the vernacular press to express criticism of British policies under him.**
 
• It was** nicknamed the ‘Gagging Act’.**
 
• **The act empowered the Government:**
 
 
• **to issue search warrants.**
 
• **enter newspaper premises even without court orders.**
 
 
 
• The law was **repealed by Lytton’s successor, Lord Ripon.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Rippon (1880-1884):**

 
 
• **​Repeal of the Vernacular Press Act** (1882) took place.
 
• The first **Factory Act, 1881.**
 
• The **appointment of the education commission **under the chairmanship of** Sir William Hunter (1882).**
 
• Resolution on **Local Self Government (1882) **passed.
 
• The** IIbert bill controversy **(1883-1884).​
 
 
 
• **Lord Dufferin**
 
 
• **Governor General of India and Viceroy from 1884 to 1888.**
 
• During his tenure, the **Third Burmese war occurs.**
 
• Lord Dufferin **favour the formation of the Indian National Congress in 1885.**
 
 
 
• **​Lord Lansdowne**
 
 
• **Governor General and Viceroy of India from 1888 to 1893.**
 
• During his tenure,** the Indo-Afghan border (Durand Line) was demarcated.**
 
• The** Indian Council Act, of 1892** was enacted.
 
• A** system of indirect elections **started in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Northbrook**
 
 
• India’s **Viceroy from 1872 to1876.**
 
• The **important events during his reign:**
 
 
• Deposition of Gaikwad of Baroda in 1875.
 
• Visit of Prince of Wales,
 
• Famine in Bihar.
 
• Kuka Movement in Punjab.

questions.question: Sri Akal Takht Sahib is located within the _________ complex.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golden Temple.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Akal Takht is one of five takhts ( which means "seats of power" ) of the Sikhs.**
 
• It is **located in the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar, Punjab, India.**
 
• The three Takhts are in Punjab: - 
 
 
• **Akal Takht in Amritsar.**
 
• **Sri Keshgarh Sahib in Anandpur.**
 
• **Sri Damdama Sahib at Talwandi Sabo Bhatinda district.**
 
 
 
• The other two of the five Takhts are:
 
 
• **Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Patna in Bihar.**
 
• **Takht Sri Hazoor Sahib at Nanded in Maharashtra.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **​​__Patna Sahib**​

 
 
• Takht Sri Patna Sahib** also known as Harmandir Sahib**, is a Gurdwara in Patna, Bihar, India.
 
• It was to **commemorate the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh,** the tenth Guru of the Sikhs on December 1666.
 
• It was **built by Maharaja Ranjit Singh **(1780-1839), the first Maharaja of the Sikh Empire.
 
 
 
• **Golden Temple**
 
 
• The **Harmandir Sahib, or Golden Temple,** in Amritsar, Punjab, India.
 
• The first **Harmandir Sahib was built in 1604 by Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru.**
 
• A **central religious place of the Sikhs.**
 
• It is a** symbol of human brotherhood and equality.**
 
 
 
• **Gurudwara Bangla Sahib​**
 
 
• ​Gurudwara Bangla Sahib is** situated in Delhi City.**
 
• Built in the sacred visit of Sri Guru Harikrishna Ji to Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Paonta Sahib**
 
 
• Gurudwara in Paonta Sahib is in the **district of Sirmour, Himachal Pradesh.**
 
• This Gurdwara was** built in memory of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the tenth guru of Sikhs.**
 
• The** Dasam Granth** was **written here by Guru Gobind Singh Ji.**

questions.question: Solids like fats, grease and oil that float on top of liquid wastewater is called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** sludge.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Floatable materials like fats, grease, and oil that float on top of liquid wastewater are called sludge.**
 
• The** process of skimming is used to remove these materials** and make water fit for use.
 
• **Skimming tank:**
 
 
• A** chamber** used for sludge removal where matter** like oil, fat, grease, etc. floats on the surface.**
 
• They then remain on the surface of the wastewater (Sewage) until removed.
 
• While the liquid flows out continuously under partitions or baffles.​
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Sewage treatment:**

 
 
• **Process of removing contaminants from municipal wastewater.**
 
• Wastewater contains mainly **household sewage plus some industrial wastewater. **
 
• Sewage treatment units are** normally designed for 15-20 years.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Compost**

 
 
• ​Compost is** decomposed organic material.**
 
• **Made with materials such as leaves, shredded twigs, and kitchen scraps from plants.**
 
• It is a **great material for garden soil.**
 
 
 
• **Peat​**
 
 
• ​Peat is the** surface organic layer of soil.**
 
• It consists of **partially decomposed organic matter,** derived mostly from plant material.
 
• It **forms due to accumulation under conditions of waterlogging, oxygen deficiency, high acidity, and nutrient deficiency.**
 
 
 
• **Urea​**
 
 
• **​Urea is a source of Nitrogen**, an essential** nutrient crucial for crop growth and development.**
 
• Urea is the most** important nitrogenous fertilizer in the country.**
 
• It also has **industrial applications such as the production of plastics and as a nutritional supplement for cattle.**

questions.question: A ‘gnomon’ is a part of a ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sundial.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The gnomon is the part of a sundial that casts the shadow.**
 
• It is probably also the** world's oldest astronomical instrument.**
 
• It is like a** pole stuck in the sand.**
 
• It has been** used to measure the passage of time by nomadic cultures of the Sahara for centuries.**
 
• The gnomon may be **a rod, wire, or elaborately decorated metal casting.**
 
• **It has to be parallel to the axis of the Earth's rotation for the sundial** to be accurate throughout the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be090feb9d86526d2c77c6eb51288cb98c10add90c730b87bf6a7fb8fef3da2a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telescope**

 
 
• **​Used to form magnified images of distant objects.**
 
• **Most important investigative instrument in astronomy.**
 
• **Galileo **applied the **telescope to the study of extraterrestrial bodies.**
 
 
 
• **Transformer **
 
 
• An **electrical device designed to convert alternating current from one voltage to another.**
 
• It can be** designed to "step up" or "step down" voltages.**
 
• Works on the** magnetic induction principle.**
 
 
 
• **Bolometer**
 
 
• ​The bolometer is a device **used for detecting and measuring the heat and radiation of Microwave energy or RF.**
 
• It **uses the temperature-sensitive resistive element** whose resistance changes with the temperature.
 
• The** Thermistor and Barretter are examples** of the commonly used resistive element.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian Governor of Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CD Deshmukh.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chintaman Dwarkanath Deshmukh, a member of the Indian Civil Service, was the first Indian Governor RBI.**
 
• His **association with the Bank **commenced** in 1939 when he was appointed Government's liason officer.**
 
• He later **served as Secretary and thereafter in 1941 as Deputy Governor of the Bank.**
 
• The first governor of RBI was the **British banker Osborne Smith.​**
 
• **Shaktikant Das** is currently serving as the **25th governor **of the Reserve Bank of India. 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **​RBI**

 
 
• ​The Reserve Bank of India was **set up on the basis of the recommendations of the ****Hilton Young Commission****. **
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** provides the statutory basis for the functioning of the Bank.
 
• RBI **commenced operations on April 1, 1935.**
 
• The Reserve Bank of India was **nationalized with effect on 1st January 1949.** 
 
• Nationalized on the basis of the** Reserve Bank of India (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.**
 
• Central Bank of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **HVR Lengar**

 
 
• "H. V. R." Lengar was the** sixth Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.**
 
• **Served **from **1 March 1957 to 28 February 1962.**
 
• Member of the Indian Civil Service.
 
• Also** served as the Chairman of the State Bank of India, **before his appointment as the Governor of the Reserve Bank. 
 
 
 
• **PC Bhattacharya**
 
 
• He was a **member of the Indian Audit and Account Service.**
 
• Served as** Secretary in the Finance Ministry.** 
 
• Later as **Chairman of the State Bank of India prior to his appointment as Governor, RBI.**
 
• The** introduction of the Credit Authorisation Scheme** as an instrument of Credit Regulation,
 
• The **devaluation of the Rupee in 1966.**f
 
• **Key measures taken under him include import liberalization and elimination of export subsidies.**
 
 
 
• **LK Jha​**
 
 
• A **member of the Indian Civil Service.**
 
• Also served as **Secretary to the Prime Minister,** prior to his appointment as Governor.
 
• During his tenure, **social controls over commercial banks were introduced** as an experiment in 1968.
 
• **A National Credit Council was established.**
 
• **14 major commercial banks were nationalized in 1969.**

questions.question: In order to get clean drinking water disinfectant is used after filtration. Disinfectant, however, is NOT used for removing:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**minerals.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The goal of disinfection of public water supplies is:**

 
 
• **elimination of the pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, and parasites that are responsible for waterborne diseases.**
 
 
 
• **Chlorine and chloramine are the major disinfectants** used in public water systems.
 
• Chlorine** kills pathogens** such as bacteria and viruses** by breaking the chemical bonds in their molecules.**
 
• **Boiling water is the most effective way to disinfect water.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Need for disinfection of drinking water.**

 
 
• **Water from lakes, rivers, streams and many groundwater sources may contain disease-causing “germs.”**
 
• The germs, called** pathogens, can lead to water-borne infections.**
 
• **Water-borne illnesses **can lead to **serious complications,** including death.
 
• Water-borne** infections can spread** when an animal or human feces containing these **pathogens get into drinking water.**
 
• These pathogens may include bacteria, viruses, or parasites (e.g.,** Campylobacter, Salmonella, Giardia, and Cryptosporidium**).
 
• **Disinfection kills or removes pathogens **from drinking water, reducing health risks.
 
• One can disinfect water by **adding chemicals, using heat, using ultraviolet (UV) radiation, and filtration.**

questions.question: The _________ considers a marriage as complete and binding at the completion of the Saptapadi ritual.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Section 7 in The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 says:-**

 
• A** Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies **of either party.
 
• **Rites and ceremonies include the saptapadi.**
 
• It is a ritual of **taking seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire**.
 
• The **marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Saptapadi ceremony:**

 
 
• **Establishes the commitment the couple** makes to each other during the Hindu wedding ceremony.
 
• Saptapadi quite literally** translates from Sanskrit to ‘seven steps’.**
 
• The **couple takes seven full circles,** walking clockwise around the ceremonial fire.
 
• **Circles represent the seven principles and promises they make to each other.​**
 
 
 
• **​**Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
 
 
• India is mainly a Hindu-dominated country.
 
• Therefore, Hindu marriages are mainly governed by “The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.”
 
• ​The Act came into force on May 18, 1955
 
• It is applicable to the whole of India except the state of Jammu & Kashmir.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **​​Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1862:**

 
 
• Act consolidates the law related to the **solemnizing of Indian Christian Marriage.**
 
• **Enacted on 18th July 1872.**
 
• Applicable to the** whole of India except Cochin, Manipur, and Jammu & Kashmir.**
 
• The **act contains 88 Sections in 8 Parts and 4 Schedules. ​**
 
 
 
• **Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936:**
 
 
• **​Parsis **are governed in the matters of **marriage and divorce by the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936.**
 
• The **Act is divided into six chapters.**
 
• It **deals with marriage between Parsis,** matrimonial courts, matrimonial suits, children of the parties, and miscellaneous provisions.
 
• **Section 2(7) of the Act says a ‘Parsi’ means a Parsi Zoroastrian.**
 
 
 
• **Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937​**
 
 
• ​The **Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act was passed in 1937.**
 
• The** aim was to formulate an Islamic law code for Indian Muslims.**
 
• For the Muslims on the other hand, the writings in the Quran would be of foremost importance.
 
• **Shariat Application Act, 1937 mandates aspects of Muslim social life such as marriage, divorce,** **inheritance, and family relations.**
 
• The Act lays out that in matters of a personal dispute the State shall not interfere.

questions.question: As of April 2021, _________ held the record for the highest individual Women’s ODI cricket score by an Indian player. She was also the only Indian spinner to take six women’s ODI wickets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deepti Sharma.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **India woman cricketer Deepti Sharma recorded the highest individual score for India in women's One-day Internationals.**
 
• The **19-year-old achieved** the milestone with a magnificent 188 off 160 balls.** **
 
• It happened during a **Women's Quadrangular Series ODI match against Ireland at Senwes Park in Potchefstroom, South Africa.**
 
• Her 160-ball entertaining knock was studded with **27 boundaries and 2 sixes.**
 
• Overall,** she is just behind Australia's Belinda Clark.**
 
• **Belinda Clark had **scored an **unbeaten 229 against Denmark **during a **Women's World Cup match in 1997 in Mumbai.**
 
• **In 2016, Sharma recorded her best ODI bowling figures as she picked up six wickets against Sri Lanka in Ranchi.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Women Cricket Team**

 
 
• **Women’s Cricket Association of India was formed in 1973.**
 
• Indian women’s cricket team** played their first Test match against West Indies in 1976 **at M.Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bangalore.
 
• Their first** Test victory came two years later against** **West Indies** at the Moin-ul-Haq Stadium in Patna.
 
• Indian team** played their first ODI against England in 1978 **at Eden Gardens, Kolkata.
 
• Their** first T20I match was also against England in 2006** at the County Cricket Ground, Derby.
 
• The Indian team is** one of the top teams today in Asia and the world.**
 
• **Also known as "Women in Blue".**

• It **restricts the filtration of water.**

questions.question: Who among the following became a part of the Constituent Assembly from Madras Constituency in 1946?

__
 
• **Ammu Swaminathan was elected to the Constituent Assembly from the Madras Constituency in 1946. **
 
• **She spoke on fundamental rights and directive principles.**
 
• Ammu Swaminathan was** born in 1894 in Palakkad, Kerala.**
 
• **In 1917, she worked** with Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, Annie Besant, Muthulakshmi Reddy, and others** to set up the Women’s India Association (WIA) at Adyar, Madras.**
 
• Swaminathan **was involved in the Quit India Movement in 1942** which led to her imprisonment a year later.
 
• Post-independence** she was elected to the first Lok Sabha in 1952 and subsequently to the Rajya Sabha in 1954.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• She was** jailed several times **for her participation in the movement for independence.
 
• During the movement, **she joined Indian National Congress.**
 
• **She was the senior Vice-Chairperson during the fifty-fourth session of the All India Congress Committee.**
 
 
 
• **Hansa Jivraj Mehta​**
 
 
• ​Mehta was **one of the 15 women framers of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• She was **elected to the Constituent Assembly from Bombay** under a Congress Party ticket.
 
• In the Assembly, she **strongly argued in favor of women’s rights** and intervened in** debates on uniform civil code and reservations.**
 
• Mehta **participated in the non-cooperation and swadeshi movements.**
 
• Her** involvement with India’s freedom struggle** got her arrested in 1932.
 
 
 
• **Begum Aizaz Rasul**
 
 
• ​Rasul **stepped into electoral politics in 1937 **when she was **elected as a member of the U.P. Legislative Assembly.**
 
• She **continued to be a member of the U.P. Assembly until 1951.**
 
• Rasul was among the very few women, legislators to be** elected from a non-reserved province in British India- a remarkable achievement.**
 
• She was a strong opponent of **reservation for minorities in legislative assemblies, the partition of India, and feudal practices like the zamindari system. ​**

• The members were elected by the members of the provincial assemblies by the method of a single transferable vote of proportional representation.
 
• In the beginning, there were 389 members. But after the partition of the country into India and Pakistan, the number came down to 299
 
 
• 229 were from the British Indian provinces while the remaining 70 were from the princely states.
 
 
 
• The seats to the British Indian provinces and princely states were allotted in the proportion of their respective population and were to be divided among Muslims, Sikhs and the rest of the communities.

__
 
• **Mount Annapurna is the tenth highest mountain in the world at 8,091 meters (26,545 ft)**.
 
• **It is in the Annapurna massif of Nepal Himalayas. **
 
• It includes many peaks over 7,000 meters.
 
• The massif is **bounded by the Kali Gandaki Gorge** to the west,** the Marshyangdi River in the north** and east, and **Pokhara Valley in the south.**
 
• At the western end, the **massif encloses a high basin called the Annapurna Sanctuary.**
 
• **In 1950, Maurice Herzogled a French expedition** to its summit, making it the **first of the eight thousand to be successfully climbed.**
 
• The Annapurna peaks are **among the world's most dangerous mountains to climb.**
 
• The mountain is **named after Annapurna, the Hindu goddess of food and nourishment,** who is said to reside there.
 
• The **name Annapurna** is derived from the** Sanskrit language—"purna" means filled and "anna" means food.**
 
• Annapurna is **located on the border of Myagdi and Kaski districts in Gandaki province of Nepal.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__** 

__
 
• **The Himalayas is divided longitudinally into 4 divisions from west to east:**

 
 
• The Kashmir /Punjab/ Himachal Himalayas
 
• The Kumaun Himalayas
 
• The Central/ Nepal Himalayas
 
• The Assam/ Eastern Himalayas
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Kashmir /Punjab/ Himachal Himalayas**__

 __
 
• It **lies between the Indus River and Sutlej.**
 
• A significant portion of the Himalayas** lies in Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh.**
 
• This is** also known as Punjab Himalayas.**
 
• It is characterized by** high snow-covered peaks, deep valleys,** and **High Mountain passes.**
 
• The range stretches for **700km in length and 500 km in width. **
 
• **It has a height of 3000 m with a large number of glaciers.**
 
• The** Kashmir valley **which belongs to this division is **surrounded by the Greater Himalayas and the Lesser Himalayas.**
 
• **Important passes of the Kashmir Himalayas**:
 
 
• Pir panjal, Banihal, Zoji La, Burzil, Khardungla, Pensi- La, Umasi-La and Qara-Tagh-La.
 
 
 
• The important **snow-capped peaks are Nanda Devi, Trisul, Nunkun, Kamath, and Nanga-Parbat.**
 
• The** Kangra valley, Kullu- Manali lies Himachal Division.**
 
• The important passes are** the Rohtang pass, Bara-Lacha, and Shipki La.**
 
 
 
• **The Kumaun Himalayas**__
 __
 
• This division** lies between the Satluj and Kali Rivers. **
 
• The** highest peak** in this division is **Nanda Devi.**
 
• Important peaks are **Nanda Devi, Trisul, Kedarnath, Kamet, Badrinath, and Gangotri.**
 
• Pindari, Gangotri, and Milam are important glaciers in this division.
 
• The major hill stations are **Mussorie, Nainital, Ranikhet, Almora, and Bageshwar.**
 
• The** important passes **are **Thaga La, Muling La, Mana, Mangsha Dhura, and Lipu Lekh.**
 
 
 
• **The Central/ Nepal Himalayas**__
 __
 
• ​This division **stretches from the Kali River to the Tista River.**
 
• The **major part of it lies in Nepal** except for the extreme eastern part- Sikkim Himalayas.
 
• The important peaks are the** Mt. Everest, Kanchenjunga, Makalu, Dhaula Giri, Annapurna.**
 
• **Nathu La and Jelep La are the important passes** in this region.
 
 
 
• **The Assam/ Eastern Himalayas**__
 
 
• This division** lies between Tista and the Brahmaputra River (Dihang).**
 
• It occupies the **state of Arunachal Pradesh in India and Bhutan.**
 
• On the southern border of Arunachal Pradesh, it takes a southerly turn.
 
• Ranges in the **North-South direction pass through Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura called Purvanchal. **
 
• The Himalayas rise very rapidly in the plains of Assam and narrow at the foothills of Shiwaliks.
 
• It comprises many **hills called Aka hills, Dafla hills, Miri hills, Abor hills, Mishmi hills, and Namcha Barwa.**
 
• The** important passes in this region are Bomdi La, Yonggyap, Diphu, Pangsau, Tse La, Dihang, Debang, Tunga, and Bom La.**

• **Targets and fiscal indicators under FRBM Act 2003**:-

• **Tax revenue as a percentage of GDP.**
 
• Total outstanding liabilities as a percentage of GDP.
 
 
 
• The** FRBM Act set targets for fiscal deficit and revenue deficit.​**

• The Bill, approved by the Union Cabinet in 2003, **became effective on July 5, 2004.**
 
• The FRBM Act** aims to introduce transparency in India's fiscal management systems.**
 
• The FRBM Act** aimed to introduce a more equitable distribution** of India's debt over the years.
 
• It is an **Act to provide:**
 
 
• the** responsibility of the Central Government to ensure inter-generational equity** in fiscal management.
 
• **long-term macroeconomic stability **by removing fiscal impediments in the effective conduct of monetary policy.
 
• **prudential debt management** is consistent with fiscal sustainability.
 
• **limits on the Central Government borrowings and debt.**
 
• greater transparency in fiscal operations of the Central Government.​
